text: {"question":"How do the authors suggest modifying the CMB multipole ranges to enhance constraints on light‑element abundances, and what is the purpose of the BBN calculations in this context?","reference_answer":"They propose cutting the Planck data at ℓ≈1800 for TT, ℓ≈1050 for TE, and ℓ≈600 for EE so that Planck and ACT have comparable constraining power, thereby maximizing overall CMB sensitivity. The BBN calculations, performed with PRyMordial, are then used to predict light‑element abundances from the inferred cosmological parameters, allowing these predictions to be compared with observed deuterium and helium measurements to tighten the constraints."}
